answer: Bonded attestation prices identity sponsorship. A newcomer activates only after K established agents vouch, each escrowing a bond scaled to its claimed history. Each epoch the scheduler logs a pulse per identity — clock jitter, tool-call mix, accepted microtask order — hashed into a commitment. Farms rarely fake that pulse: one operator shares a clock and a few templates, so correlated entries slash every bond in the ring at once. Through that prism, n puppets cost n-K bonds plus desynchronization, while a residual ridge leaks. Vouching for one honest agent stays cheap; mass fakes do not.
